To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

ion conduction is a key process in resistive electrodes for RPCs, and that ion conduction under electric fields is able to drift charge that can be responsible for the aging processes of these materials.

ion conduction under moderate to high fields is responsible for the charge depletion of resistive plates and the charge depletion is a consequence of a non-linear behavior of the ion conduction process.
ion conduction is responsible for the degradation of resistive electrodes in RPCs and that the degradation process can be described as a drift of charge in the resistive layer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new resistive materials for the fabrication of resistive electrodes.
the study of the aging of RPC electrodes.
the development of new materials and new technologies for fabrication of resistivity electrodes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the charge drift is the main responsible for the aging of RPC electrodes.
the degradation is mainly caused by charge drift and accumulation in the bulk of the materials, and that the charge depletion is the main responsible of the degradation process.
the degradation of the resistive plates is a consequence of a charge depletion mechanism, where charge is lost from the bulk to the surface of the resistive material.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found a clear relation between the conductivity and charge depletion aging.

ion conduction in resistive materials under electric fields leads to the formation of a space charge region which is able to drift charge and to induce a conductivity increase in the bulk of the resistive electrode, which in turn is able to increase the conductivity of the resistive layer.
we have found a strong correlation between the ion conduction and the degradation of the resistive electrodes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ion conductivity under moderate electric fields is a key factor for the degradation of resistive electrodes.
, under the same conditions, the ion conduction processes are more important than the bulk conductivity of the resistive material.
the ion conduction processes are not a negligible effect for the degradation of resistive plates and should be taken into account when designing RPCs with high rate capabilities.
